typeName: Q3: Inference (a test or an interval)
title: Has nightly homework dropped? A one-proportion z test

stimulus.title: Homework survey of high school seniors
stimulus.html:
Three years ago, a state survey found that 40% of the state's high school seniors did at least one hour of homework on a typical school night. Education officials believe this proportion has gone down. This year they selected a random sample of 600 of the state's 120,000 seniors; 213 of them said they do at least one hour of homework on a typical school night. The officials will use a significance level of α=0.05\alpha = 0.05.

Survey results this year (invented data)
Seniors sampledAt least one hour of homeworkSample proportion
600213p^=0.355\hat{p} = 0.355

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate significance test by name, and state the null and alternative hypotheses, defining the parameter in context.

rubric.point: Names the procedure as a one-sample z test for a proportion (one-proportion z test)
accept: one-sample z test for a population proportion
1-proportion z test
a z test for one proportion

rubric.point: States H_0: p = 0.40 and H_a: p < 0.40, written about the parameter p (not p-hat)
accept: words equivalent to these hypotheses, with the null value 0.40 and a one-sided less-than alternative

rubric.point: Defines p in context as the true proportion of all the state's high school seniors who do at least one hour of homework on a typical school night (this year)
accept: p = the proportion of all seniors in the state this year who do 1+ hour of homework a night
p = the population proportion of the state's seniors who do at least an hour of homework

parts.sample: One-sample z test for a proportion. H_0: p = 0.40 and H_a: p < 0.40, where p = the true proportion of all the state's high school seniors this year who do at least one hour of homework on a typical school night.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Justify that the conditions for this test are met.

rubric.point: Random and 10%: the officials took a random sample, and 600 is less than 10% of the 120,000 seniors
accept: random sample stated; 600 < 0.10(120,000) = 12,000
both the random condition and the 10% condition checked in words with numbers

rubric.point: Large counts with the null value: n p_0 = 600(0.40) = 240 and n(1 - p_0) = 600(0.60) = 360 are both at least 10
accept: expected successes and failures under H_0 are at least 10 (5 is also accepted as the threshold)

parts.sample: Random: the problem says the officials selected a random sample of 600 seniors. 10%: 600 is less than 10% of the 120,000 seniors in the state (12,000). Large counts: n p_0 = 600(0.40) = 240 >= 10 and n(1 - p_0) = 600(0.60) = 360 >= 10, so the sampling distribution of p-hat is approximately normal.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the test statistic and the p-value. Show the expression you used, with the values substituted.

rubric.point: Shows the test statistic expression with p_0 in the standard error: z = (0.355 - 0.40)/sqrt(0.40(0.60)/600)
accept: (p-hat - p_0)/sqrt(p_0(1 - p_0)/n) with 0.355, 0.40 and 600 substituted
using p-hat = 0.355 inside the square root does not earn this point
a value consistent with the student's expression earns this point only if the expression used p_0

rubric.point: Reports the p-value as about 0.012, the area to the left of z = -2.25 (one-sided)
accept: p-value = 0.0122
p-value = P(Z <= -2.25) = 0.0122 from Table A
a two-sided value of about 0.024 does not earn this point

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Justify a conclusion in the context of this study, using α=0.05\alpha = 0.05.

rubric.point: Compares the p-value with alpha and makes the decision: because 0.012 < 0.05, reject H_0
accept: since the p-value of 0.0122 is less than 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis
a decision consistent with the student's p-value from part (c), with the inequality stated

rubric.point: States the conclusion with evidence language about the parameter in context: there is convincing evidence that the true proportion of all the state's seniors who do at least one hour of homework a night is less than 0.40
accept: convincing evidence that the proportion of all seniors in the state with 1+ hour of homework a night has dropped below 0.40
"proves", "accept", or a conclusion about the sample proportion does not earn this point

parts.sample: Because the p-value of 0.0122 is less than alpha = 0.05, we reject H_0. There is convincing evidence that the true proportion of all the state's high school seniors who do at least one hour of homework on a typical school night is less than 0.40.
